subject: spade and cable
title: What If One Spade Could Switch Off a Country's Internet? In 2011 It Did

scenes.text: What if one spade could knock a whole country offline? In 2011, one did.
March 28, 2011. Not far from Tbilisi, in Georgia, a 75-year-old woman is digging for scrap copper to sell.
Her spade hits a cable. It isn't copper. It's the fibre-optic line that carries about 90 percent of neighbouring Armenia's internet.
Across the border, 3.2 million people go offline for hours. Parts of Georgia and Azerbaijan drop out too.
Police held her, then released her because of her age. Local media named her the spade-hacker. She said she never cut any cable.
The line was supposed to be protected. Landslides or heavy rain may have left it exposed. A whole country's connection, one spade deep.

description:
What if a single person with a spade could take a country offline? On 28 March 2011, a 75-year-old woman scavenging for copper near Tbilisi, Georgia, damaged a fibre-optic cable owned by the Georgian railway network.
The line carried about 90 percent of Armenia's internet traffic, and 3.2 million people lost access for hours (reports range from five to twelve), with parts of Georgia and Azerbaijan affected as well. Local media called her the spade-hacker; she denied cutting the cable. Landslides or heavy rain may have exposed it.
What should we run through next?

first_comment: Reports of the outage range from five hours to twelve. How long could you last offline, and what should we run through next?
